name: Ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel
drug_class: Combined hormonal contraceptive (oestrogen plus second-generation progestin)
route_note: oral tablets daily in monophasic, triphasic or extended cycles; weekly transdermal patch

discovery.note: Combination of ethinylestradiol, the first orally active synthetic oestrogen (1938), with levonorgestrel.

rx_status: prescription (OTC or pharmacist-supplied in some countries)
tagline: Classic second-generation combined pill with a low venous thrombosis risk
summary: Ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel is a combined hormonal contraceptive pairing a synthetic oestrogen with a second-generation progestin. It is among the most widely used and studied oral contraceptives and is often recommended first-line because of its relatively low risk of venous thromboembolism among combined pills.
mechanism: The oestrogen and progestin suppress hypothalamic GnRH pulses and pituitary FSH and LH secretion, preventing follicle development and ovulation.

Levonorgestrel also thickens cervical mucus and makes the endometrium less receptive, while ethinylestradiol stabilises the endometrium for predictable bleeding. Extended-cycle regimens reduce the number of withdrawal bleeds per year.
uses: Menstrual cycle regulation and reduction of dysmenorrhoea (common use)

history.title: First pill
history.detail: FDA approves Enovid, the first oral contraceptive.

history.title: Norgestrel
history.detail: Norgestrel is synthesised; its active isomer levonorgestrel is later paired with ethinylestradiol.

history.title: UK pill scare
history.detail: UK regulators warn that pills containing third-generation progestins carry higher VTE risk than levonorgestrel pills, prompting a shift back to them.

history.title: Extended cycle
history.detail: FDA approves Seasonale, a 91-day regimen with four withdrawal bleeds a year.

history.title: Continuous use
history.detail: FDA approves Lybrel for continuous use without a hormone-free interval.

history.title: Patch
history.detail: FDA approves Twirla, a levonorgestrel–ethinylestradiol transdermal patch.

pk.metabolism: CYP3A4; sulfation and glucuronidation with enterohepatic recycling

serious: stroke and myocardial infarction (especially smokers over 35)
safety.boxed_warning: Cigarette smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular events from combined hormonal contraceptives; this risk rises with age and number of cigarettes, and use is contraindicated in women over 35 who smoke.
